intro.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Lake Oswego without the runaround
paragraphs: Straight Line Design and Remodeling has handled kitchen remodeling in Lake Oswego and the Portland west side since 2010. The pitch is simple: one team takes your project from the first sketch through engineering, permits, construction and any warranty repairs, so you are not managing five companies at once.

You also know where you stand early. The first step is a phone call with owner Matt Williams, who gives rough timeline and pricing estimates before anyone visits. Kitchen packages are published in tiers, and the 5% design retainer is credited to your contract if you build with the team. Google reviewers point to crews that kept the schedule and an owner who listened.

items.name: Kitchen Remodel
items.blurb: Better traffic flow, smarter storage and cabinets, counters, flooring and appliances picked with a designer. Updated wiring and plumbing come with it. Recent kitchens in Southwest Portland, Beaverton, Cedar Hills and West Linn have earned NARI and Oregon Home awards.

image.alt: Portland kitchen and living room remodel with navy island, white shaker cabinets, black dome pendants and leather counter stools

items.name: Bathroom Remodel
items.blurb: Bigger showers, tile that is easy to clean, heated floors and touchless faucets. Walk-in showers, grab bars and non-slip floors are built in for kids or aging parents, and designer Alicia Warming has specialized Aging in Place training.

image.alt: Lake Oswego bathroom remodel with navy vanity, white herringbone tile wall, brass faucet and frameless glass shower

items.name: Home Additions
items.blurb: New square footage designed to look like it was always part of the house, from primary suites to family rooms. The team's structural designer and architectural design manager work out the framing and permits before construction begins.

image.alt: Lake Oswego home addition with primary bedroom, wood ceiling beam, linear gas fireplace and green accent wall

items.name: ADU Design and Build
items.blurb: Backyard units for family, rental income or a quiet workspace, matched to your house or styled on their own. One Google reviewer had a detached garage torn down and replaced with a 600 square foot ADU that he now rents out.

image.alt: Portland ADU with dark green siding, shed roof, covered wood entry and horizontal cedar fence

items.name: Basement and Attic Conversions
items.blurb: Unused space under the floor or under the roof turned into bedrooms, baths and living areas. Past projects include a Portland basement with a new bathroom and a Southeast Portland attic conversion, both designed and permitted in-house.

about.h2: Meet owner and general manager Matt Williams
about.text: Matt Williams started Straight Line in 2010 and still runs the first conversation on every project. He studied building construction technology, construction management and kitchen and bath design, and today he serves as president of NARI Pacific Northwest. Off the clock he does fine woodworking. His view is that a remodel should stand the test of time and make daily life better. He works with interior design manager Nikki Ditterick, designer Alicia Warming, architectural design manager Steve Griffin, an Army veteran, and production manager Nick Johnston, who keeps communication steady once crews arrive.

image.alt: Matt Williams, owner of Straight Line Design and Remodeling in Lake Oswego, OR

process.h2: How your remodel moves from call to keys

steps.title: Call with Matt, then a site visit
steps.text: A phone call for rough timeline and pricing, then a free on-site consultation to check structure, layout options and a general estimate.

steps.title: Design retainer and concepts
steps.text: A 5% design retainer starts design. The designer shows 1 to 3 layout options, refined over 2 to 5 meetings.

steps.title: Selections, contract and permits
steps.text: You choose tile, cabinets and fixtures, review the final proposal, sign the contract and the team pulls the trade permits.

steps.title: Construction
steps.text: Zipper walls and weatherproofing contain dust while crews build. Most projects take 6 to 16 weeks of construction, depending on scope.

steps.title: Walk-through and photos
steps.text: A return visit for touch-ups after you settle in, a client survey, and professional after photos from the in-house photographer.

service_area.h2: Lake Oswego, Portland and the west-side suburbs
service_area.text: Straight Line is based in Lake Oswego and meets clients by appointment. Since 2010 the team has worked across the Portland metro area, with most projects in Lake Oswego, Portland, Beaverton, Cedar Hills, Hillsboro, Aloha, King City, Tigard, Tualatin and Sherwood. If you live nearby and are not sure you are in range, ask on your first call.

items.q: How much does a kitchen remodel cost with Straight Line?
items.a: The site publishes kitchen tiers. The Builder package runs $75,000 to $90,000 and the Semi-Designer package runs $90,000 to $110,000. Matt gives rough numbers on the first call, then a more accurate estimate after he walks your home. Both of those steps are free.

items.q: What is the design retainer and do I get it back?
items.a: The design retainer is typically 5% of the project estimate and is paid up front to start design. If you go ahead and build with Straight Line, the full amount is applied to your contract price. If you do not, it is kept as a fee for the design work.

items.q: How long will my remodel take?
items.a: Construction usually runs 6 to 16 weeks depending on scope, after design and permits. Design itself takes 2 to 5 concept meetings depending on how quickly decisions get made, and contract signing is set within 1 to 2 weeks of the final proposal meeting.

Yes. Engineering and permitting are part of the service, and the team knows the Portland permit process well. A structural designer joins the final proposal meeting, and the team secures the trade building permits before construction starts so you do not deal with the city yourself.

items.q: Can we stay home while you work?
items.a: Most families do. Before demolition the area is prepped to prevent damage, and zipper walls plus weatherproofing hold back dust and debris through construction. A detailed checklist closes out the job, and the team comes back after you settle in for any touch-ups.

final_cta.text: Tell Matt about your kitchen, bath or addition and get rough timing and pricing on the first call.
